title: DLP incident API wire behavior: list envelopes, paging, close, delete, triggers and evidence, and where the SDKs part from the contract

prose.text: These are the incident operations' behaviors beyond the generated paths and methods. The reference is the help API page; both SDKs call the same /dlp/v1/incidents family.
{{list-envelopes}} {{go-pager}} The Go pager reads the wrong member for incident lists {{divergence:go-list-member}}. {{python-transactions-envelope}}
{{search-page-params}} The Go pager starts at a different page number {{divergence:page-start}} and asks for more per page than the documented maximum {{divergence:page-size}}.
Go puts the incident ID in a different place for notes and tickets {{divergence:go-path-order}}.

{{delete-operation}} {{python-no-delete}} The portal's deletion is permanent and permission-gated, [[zwa.incidents:delete-permanent]]; whether the API delete is the same is open {{gap:delete-semantics}}.
{{triggers-v1-v2}} {{sdk-triggers-no-context}} {{sdk-triggers-no-context-param}} How a client should get trigger context is open {{gap:trigger-context}}.

{{evidence}} Go types its `additionalInfo` differently from the contract {{divergence:evidence-additional-info}}. Oversized evidence files are replaced by placeholders: [[zwa.incidents:evidence-placeholder]].

checks.do: Whether an empty Go incident search or transaction lookup is the pager reading `logs` while the response carries `incidents`.
Whether a Go list call skipped the first page, by comparing with a raw request that starts at page 0.
Whether a Go close request carried an empty resolution code the API might reject.

list-envelopes.statement: In the API reference, incident search and the transaction lookup return an incident list whose members are `cursor` and `incidents`, the tickets operation returns `cursor` and `tickets`, and the audit log search returns `cursor` and `logs`; the getting-started example reads `data["incidents"]` from a transaction lookup.

go-pager.statement: The Go `ReadAllPages` helper decodes each page's items from a `logs` member, and the Go incident search, transaction lookup and ticket lookup use it, as does the audit log search.

quotes: allResults, cursor, err := common.ReadAllPages[common.IncidentDetails](ctx, service.Client, http.MethodPost, path, paginationParams, filters)
allResults, cursor, err := common.ReadAllPages[common.IncidentDetails](ctx, service.Client, http.MethodGet, endpoint, paginationParams, nil)
allResults, cursor, err := common.ReadAllPages[Ticket](ctx, service.Client, http.MethodGet, path, paginationParams, nil)
common.ReadAllPages[AuditLog](ctx, service.Client, http.MethodPost, endpoint, paginationParams, filters)

python-transactions-envelope.statement: Python's `get_incident_transactions` builds one `IncidentDLPDetails` from the whole response body and returns it in a one-element list, while the reference returns an incident list envelope; the model reads incident fields such as `internalId` from the top level, so the incidents are not in the parsed result and must be read from the raw response.

quotes: self.internal_id = config["internalId"] if "internalId" in config else None

python-transactions-envelope.conditions: Follows from the model reading per-incident keys at the top level of a body whose top level holds only cursor and incidents per the reference; not observed against a live response.

search-page-params.statement: Incident search takes `page` (minimum 0, default 0, not needed when `pageId` is used), `pageSize` (default 10, maximum 100) and `pageId`, a page identifier returned by the first search that later requests can use instead of the page number.

expect.description: Specifies the page number of the incident in a multi-paginated response. This field is not required if page ID field is used.
Specifies the page size (i.e., number of incidents per page). The maximum page size is 100.

Specifies the page ID of the incident in a multi-paginated response. It is a unique identifier returned in the first search request. You can use the page ID instead of the page number in subsequent search requests for faster and more efficient results.

search-fields.statement: Incident search filters by exact field value or by time range; the searchable fields are severity, priority, transactionId, status, sourceDLPType, labels, incidentGroupIds and engine, the source DLP types are SaaS Security API, Email, INLINE and ENDPOINT, and a labels filter takes label names with their values.

expect.description:
Filters DLP incidents based on the given time range and the field values. The supported field values are:
  • Severity
  • Priority
  • Transaction ID
  • Status
  • Source DLP Type
    • The source DLP types that that you can use to filter and search an incident are SaaS Security API, Email, INLINE, and ENDPOINT.
  • Labels
    • To filter DLP incidents based on labels, ensure that you replace the parameter value:[string] with value:[{label_name: [label_value]}] in the request body. You need to provide the label name and its associated value to get accurate results.
  • Incident Group
  • Engine
The supported time range values are:
  • Start date and time
  • End date and time
Search request filters the DLP incidents based on the field value (exact match) or the time range (start and end time).

status-values.statement: The API's incident statuses are NEW, INVESTIGATING, VALIDATE_WITH_USER, JUSTIFICATION_RESPONSE_RECEIVED, ESCALATED and RESOLVED.

close-request.statement: The close request carries an optional `resolutionLabel`, `resolutionCode` and `notes`, and the only resolution code is FALSE_POSITIVE.

python-close.statement: Python's `incident_close` sends `resolutionLabel`, `resolutionCode` and `notes` and drops any of them left empty.

quotes: body = {k: v for k, v in body.items() if v}

go-close.statement: Go's `UpdateIncidentStatus` sets only `Notes` in its close request, whose `resolutionLabel` and `resolutionCode` members carry no omitempty option.

go-close-empty-members.statement: So a Go close always sends an empty `resolutionLabel` object and an empty-string `resolutionCode`, which is not one of the documented codes, and cannot close an incident as a false positive.
go-close-empty-members.conditions: Go's JSON encoder writes every member without omitempty, so the zero-valued label struct and string are sent; how the API treats an empty resolutionCode is not observed.

delete-operation.statement: The API reference documents DELETE on an incident as deleting the DLP incident for the given ID, returning a boolean on success, and the Go SDK's `DeleteDLPIncident` calls it.

expect.description: Deletes the DLP incident for the specified incident ID

quotes: resp, err := service.Client.NewRequestDo(ctx, "DELETE", path, nil, nil, nil)

python-no-delete.statement: The Python SDK's DLP incidents module has no delete method.
python-no-delete.conditions: Rests on every def in zscaler/zwa/dlp_incidents.py at the pin: __init__, get_incident_transactions, get_incident_details, change_history, get_incident_triggers, get_generated_tickets, get_incident_evidence, dlp_incident_search, incident_group_search, assign_labels, incident_notes and incident_close.

triggers-v1-v2.statement: The v1 triggers operation, which downloads the data that triggered the incident, is marked deprecated; a v2 operation returns the trigger metadata nested by source category. Both take `fetchTriggerContext`, which on v1 adds the prefix and suffix data when true and defaults to false.

expect.description: Downloads the actual data that triggered the incident

(Optional) Specifies whether to download the complete incident trigger data, including the prefix and suffix information. Set this field to true to fetch the prefix and suffix data.The default value is false.
Downloads the actual trigger metadata of the incident in a nested structure organized by source category.
Boolean value indicating whether to fetch trigger data context

sdk-triggers-no-context.statement: The Python `get_incident_triggers` takes only `incident_id` and builds a request to the triggers path under its `/zwa/dlp/v1` base with no query parameters; the Go `GetDLPIncidentTriggers` takes only the incident ID and sends a GET to the triggers path under `/dlp/v1/incidents` with nil options.

quotes: func GetDLPIncidentTriggers(ctx context.Context, service *services.Service, dlpIncidentID string) (DLPIncidentTriggerData, *http.Response, error) {
resp, err := service.Client.NewRequestDo(ctx, "GET", path, nil, nil, &triggers)

sdk-triggers-no-context-param.statement: So neither SDK can send `fetchTriggerContext`, and both reach only the v1 triggers operation.
sdk-triggers-no-context-param.conditions: Read from the two functions at the pin: neither takes an argument that becomes a query parameter. Not observed on the wire.

evidence.statement: The evidence operation returns the incident's evidence URL, which views and downloads an XML file with the data that triggered the incident, together with `fileName`, `fileType` and `additionalInfo`.

expect.description: Gets the evidence URL of the incident. You can use the evidence link to view and download the XML file with the actual data that triggered the incident.

fileType.description: The type or extension of the file

additionalInfo.description: Any additional information about the incident

evidenceURL.description: The evidence URL of the incident

go-list-member.summary: The reference returns incident and ticket lists under `incidents` and `tickets`, while the Go pager reads items only from `logs`.

positions.says: Incident search and transaction lookups return cursor and incidents; ticket lookups return cursor and tickets.
The Go pager's page struct maps its items to logs.

go-list-member.impact: If responses follow the reference, Go's FilterIncidentSearch, GetIncidentTransactions and GetDLPIncidentTickets return no items with no error, because the JSON decoder ignores the unmatched incidents and tickets members; the audit log search, whose list is logs, is unaffected. Not observed against a live tenant.

page-start.summary: The reference's page numbers start at 0, while the Go pager starts at page 1 unless the caller sets one.

positions.says: Incident search's page parameter has minimum 0 and default 0.
ReadAllPages starts at page 1 and stops once the page number reaches totalPages minus 1.

page-start.impact: If pages are numbered from 0, a Go list call without an explicit page skips the first page of results. Not observed.

page-size.summary: Incident search documents a maximum page size of 100, and Python's docstrings say the same for search and audit logs, while the Go pager requests 1000 per page by default.

expect.description: Specifies the page size (i.e., number of incidents per page). The maximum page size is 100.

positions.says: Python documents page_size with Max: 100 for the audit log search.

quotes: Specifies the page size (i.e., number of incidents per page). Max: 100.

page-size.impact: A Go list call without PageSize asks for 1000 items a page; whether the server caps, rejects or honors it is not observed. The audit log operation in the reference states no maximum.

go-path-order.summary: Go adds notes at /incidents/notes/{id} and reads tickets at /incidents/tickets/{id}, while the reference and Python put the ID first: /incidents/{id}/notes and /incidents/{id}/tickets.

positions.says: The reference's note and ticket operations are under the incident ID.

expect.description: Adds notes to the incident during updates or status changes

positions.says: Go formats the notes and tickets paths with the ID last.

go-path-order.impact: Go's CreateNotes and GetDLPIncidentTickets call paths the reference does not list; unless the server also accepts them, those two functions fail.

evidence-additional-info.summary: The reference types evidence `additionalInfo` as an object, while Go types it as a string.

expect.description: Any additional information about the incident

positions.says: Go's DLPIncidentEvidence declares AdditionalInfo as a string.

evidence-additional-info.impact: If the API returns an object, Go's JSON decoding of the evidence response fails with a type error; the incident details' application and content additionalInfo, also strings in Go, appear as objects in the getting-started example. Not observed.

delete-semantics.title: Whether the API delete matches the portal's permanent, permission-gated delete
delete-semantics.detail: The portal says deletion is permanent and needs a role with delete access for Incidents, and the API reference says DELETE deletes the incident. Not stated: whether an API key's role needs the same permission, whether the API delete is equally unrecoverable, and why Python has no delete.
delete-semantics.blocks: deciding whether an API client may delete incidents safely

trigger-context.title: How an SDK user gets trigger context, and when to move to v2 triggers
trigger-context.detail: Neither SDK can send fetchTriggerContext or call the v2 triggers path, and the v1 path is deprecated. Open: whether the SDKs will add either, and whether v2 returns the same data in a new shape.
trigger-context.blocks: fetching prefix and suffix trigger context from an SDK
